messages:
elaine: Quick thread: proposing a slightly different take on scoped API keys - 'signed scopes' that are HMAC-signed at creation time so edges can validate without needing full policy sync. Thinking about migration, replay-protection, and exceptions for batch jobs. Thoughts?
marco: Interesting. So keys carry a compact signed payload like {svc, proj, routes, exp, nonce} and edge verifies signature + expiry. That avoids per-request policy lookup.
tariq: Signature verification at edge is great for latency, but key revocation becomes harder. How do we revoke immediately if a key leaks?
elaine: We can combine short max-ttl for signed scopes (e.g., 24h) + a revocation blacklist cached at edge with bloom filter updates. Bloom filter updates are ~small and can be pushed via CDN invalidation.
marco: Bloom filters solve scalable revocation but false positives could block valid keys. Need metrics for false positive rate and a fast fallback path to auth service.
tariq: Also consider replay: add a nonce/window that edges check against a lightweight cache (LRU) for recent nonces. For high QPS, that cache could be heavy. Maybe rely on short TTL + optional per-request nonce only for write routes.
elaine: Good point. We can start by applying nonce checks only to mutating endpoints and let read routes accept time-bound signed scopes without nonce checks.
marco: How about background jobs? They often run from VMs without token exchange. We could allow a special long-lived signed scope but only if the key is pinned to a workload identity (attested via instance metadata signature at mint time).
tariq: Need an attestation flow: job requests a signed scope from key-management service (KMS) providing workload cert; KMS mints signed scope with shorter TTL and records attestation. That gives audit trail and binds key to host.
elaine: Migration path idea: 1) Mint signed-scopes as opt-in meta on existing keys. 2) Roll out edge signature verifier in observe mode (log but accept). 3) Push a small blacklist service + bloom sync. 4) Start canary enforcing for select routes.
marco: DB changes: add signed_scope_blob and attestation_records table. Keep old api_keys rows unchanged to allow dual-accept.
tariq: Telemetry: count of signature failures, revoked-but-used events, attestation failures, edge-fallback rate. Dashboards and an alert if fallback > 1% p95.
elaine: Security tradeoffs: signed scopes reduce real-time policy flexibility (can't change scope unless key reissued). But they give great edge performance and scale. We'll need a clear owner-runbook for emergency key revocation.
marco: Ops notes: implement verifier in edge as a tiny WASM plugin so we can push to CDN in a single patch. Keeps latency <1ms.
tariq: We should also add a server-side exchange endpoint for long-lived keys to request short-lived signed scopes for server workloads that can't do interactive exchange. That endpoint must be rate-limited + audited.
devops-bot: deploy:edge-verifier v0.1 scheduled for infra-canary at 2025-04-02T02:00Z.
elaine: Action items: Elaine to write a one-pager comparing signed-scopes vs token-exchange (due Wed). Marco to prototype WASM verifier (POC in 5d). Tariq to draft attestation API + revocation bloom sync design (PR in 4d).
marco: Also will add a small traffic experiment: enable verifier in observe on /v1/embeddings for 72h to validate signatures and false-positive revokes.	ariq: +1. If we see high false positives on bloom revokes, fallback to immediate per-key pulls for affected canary only.
elaine: Thanks team. Will schedule a short sync after POCs.
